transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I came because my talking… it gets all tangled up. I start trying to tell somebody one thing, like about the keys, and then somehow I’m talking about jail, and then the prayer rug, and then chess pieces—like the little horse one, you know—and people look at me like they don’t know where I went. They say they can’t follow me. I’m trying to explain it right, but it comes out mixed.
Have you been feeling unusually high or excited lately?

Yeah… yeah, sometimes I get like that. Like I feel real up, like I’m bigger than the room, you know? I’ll be laughing loud, talking to everybody, like the whole building can hear me—when I’m mopping the hallway, even, I’ll be joking with folks like I’m running the place.

But then if somebody says, “Why you talking like that?” or looks at me wrong, I can get mad fast. Like snap, shouting over nothing, like a little thing. It’s like the high feeling turns sharp.
When your mood feels normal—not especially high or low—do you still have times when your thoughts get tangled up like that?

Yeah… even when I’m not all up or mad or nothing, it still happens. I’ll be feeling regular, just trying to say something simple—like where the keys are—and then my mouth goes somewhere else, talking about jail, then that prayer rug, then chess pieces, the little horse one… and I can see people’s faces change. They tell me, “I can’t follow what you’re saying,” but in my head I was trying to make it make sense.
Do you ever hear voices when no one is there?

Yeah… I do. Not all the time, but sometimes I hear this man’s voice, like it’s coming out the vents, or from over by the mop closet. And I’ll check, because you know, in the building sounds travel funny—pipes knocking, people upstairs dragging chairs, all that—but it’s like he says my name. Or he’ll say I ruined everything.

And it sounds real, like somebody standing right beside me, not like just thinking it. Then I’m looking around with the mop in my hand, feeling stupid, because nobody’s there.
Have you had a time when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know about counting the exact days, but there’s been stretches where most days I wake up and it’s like… heavy. Like after morning prayer I’ll just sit on the edge of the bed, not moving, just staring.

And I know I’m supposed to get up, wash up, go outside, do what I gotta do, but it feels empty. Like what’s the point of cleaning myself up if I’m just gonna feel the same. Then I start thinking about the hallway needing mopping, and the bucket with the wheel that sticks—see, that thing been broken forever—but I’m still just sitting there, like I can’t get myself started.
Have there been at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice even though you were not feeling especially high or depressed?

Yeah… yeah, that’s happened. Like I wasn’t feeling all charged up or real down in the bed or nothing, just kind of regular weeks, going to work, sweeping, taking out trash… and I still heard him.

More than two weeks, I think. The man in the vents, saying things, and I’d be looking up at those little grates like—well, you know how dust collects there, nobody cleans them right unless I get the ladder—but anyway, I’d hear him. And I’d still feel like people in the building were signaling about me, like little looks or noises meant something. Even when my mood wasn’t the problem.
Have you ever had a period when your mood was so high or irritable that you barely needed sleep?

Yeah… there been times like that. I’ll sleep maybe two, three hours, and then I’m up before the sun like I had a full night, feeling fresh, ready to go.

And it’s not like normal waking up, you know? I start thinking about all the work I can get done—floors, trash rooms, the supply closet, how I should move things around so it runs better. Like sleep is for other people, not me. Then I’m already making plans before anybody else is even out the bed.
